name: Calendly
summary: Your own account can connect to a sandbox OAuth app quickly, but external users need a Production app that meets Calendly's developer policy, with an HTTPS redirect and a privacy policy plus support instructions. I found no official OAuth review queue, so whether Calendly must approve a Production app (or a partner listing) is the decision that sets the real timeline and needs to be confirmed with Calendly first.

verdict.label: Moderate
verdict.timeToFirstConnection: About 0.5 to 1 day of your hands-on work (my estimate). No provider wait is documented for a sandbox app.
verdict.timeToProduction: Unknown. Your hands-on work is roughly 2 to 5 days (my estimate). The provider-side step is not documented in the official OAuth pages I read.
verdict.approvalWait: Official pages describe no review queue for a Production OAuth app. A partner-program application exists, but its timing is not published. One secondary report describes credentials returned within one business day, but that was in a different integrator's flow. No firm Calendly review timeline was found.
verdict.handsOnEffort: Sandbox app and an end-to-end test with your own account: a few hours. Production readiness: privacy policy, support instructions, HTTPS redirect, a minimal scope set, and token-refresh handling. Partner application if you want listing.

decideFirst.question: Will one account connect, or many users?
decideFirst.guidance: Calendly's overview says OAuth is required when multiple accounts connect, while personal access tokens suit installs into a single account. If only your own company's account will ever be used, a personal access token avoids OAuth entirely.

decideFirst.question: Sandbox or Production app, and which redirect URI?
decideFirst.guidance: Start with a Sandbox app. Sandbox redirect URIs can be http on localhost, while Production redirect URIs must be https. Calendly recommends a second Production app when real customer data is involved.

decideFirst.question: Which scopes will you request?
decideFirst.guidance: Request the minimum set. New OAuth apps get no API access until scopes are requested and approved, and a missing scope returns a 403. Examples from the catalog include scheduled_events:read and webhooks:write, and webhooks need the related read scopes.

phases.name: 1 · Prove the flow with your own account
phases.goal: Complete the authorization-code flow with PKCE using a Sandbox app and your own Calendly account.

steps.title: Log in to Calendly and open Developer tools
steps.detail: Use the Profile menu's Developer item, or manage apps at developer.calendly.com if the item is missing while accounts migrate.

steps.title: Create a Sandbox OAuth app
steps.detail: Set the app name (letters, numbers, hyphens and spaces only), enter exactly one redirect URI, choose Sandbox, then select at least one scope.

steps.title: Save the client ID, client secret and webhook signing key immediately
steps.detail: The client secret and webhook signing key cannot be viewed again after creation, and the client ID cannot be viewed again in Developer tools either.

steps.title: Implement PKCE and the token exchange
steps.detail: Generate a code verifier, derive an S256 challenge, redirect the user to the authorize endpoint, then exchange the code at the token endpoint. Server apps also send the client secret using HTTP Basic authentication.

steps.title: Test the token against the current-user endpoint
steps.detail: Calendly's own test step calls the Get current user endpoint with the new access token.

phases.name: 2 · Prepare the app for other users
phases.goal: Create a Production app and meet the developer-policy items Calendly publishes, before any outside user connects.
phases.duration: About 2 to 5 days of hands-on work (my estimate), excluding any provider wait

steps.title: Write a privacy policy that covers your data use
steps.detail: Calendly's developer policy requires an industry-standard privacy policy that accurately describes data usage and meets applicable legal and consent requirements.

steps.title: Publish connection instructions and a support contact
steps.detail: The developer policy says the application must include instructions on how to connect Calendly and customer support information. It also asks that the app follow Calendly brand guidelines.

steps.title: Create the Production app with an https redirect and minimal scopes
steps.detail: Production redirect URIs must be https. Use a callback on a domain you control, and request only the scopes the features need.

steps.title: Test refresh-token rotation and revocation handling
steps.detail: Each refresh invalidates the old refresh token, so store the new one every time. Handle invalid_grant by sending the user through authorization again.

steps.title: Ask Calendly whether production or partner review applies to you
steps.detail: Partner program applications are made through Calendly's partner portal, and the requirements appear to include a relevant audience or a maintained integration. Confirm in writing whether an OAuth Production app needs approval before you launch.

evidence.note: Partner program sources are secondary. Official OAuth pages do not describe this step.

phases.name: 3 · Provider decision (only if Calendly requires it)
phases.goal: Get Calendly's go-ahead for external users or a partner listing.

steps.title: Wait for Calendly's partner or marketplace decision
steps.detail: A developer on Calendly's community asked whether a marketplace submission needs extra validation. The excerpt I saw shows no answer.

evidence.note: Community question only; no official answer found.

steps.title: Confirm the app works for a non-owner account before launch
steps.detail: Have a second Calendly account connect and disconnect, and check that scoped calls and webhooks behave as expected.

evidence.note: Testing advice is my own recommendation, not from a source.

requirements.requiredFor: Creating OAuth apps in Developer tools
requirements.note: Official docs say you log in or sign up. A Workato page says developer accounts are separate from your Calendly user account, so confirm which one you use.

requirements.requiredFor: Making API calls with a connected account
requirements.note: Apideck says free Basic accounts have limited API access. This is not on the official pages I read.

requirements.item: Https redirect URI on a domain you control
requirements.note: Domain control is my inference from the https rule. Confirm your DNS setup before creating the Production app.

requirements.requiredFor: Every OAuth app, Sandbox or Production

requirements.item: Connection instructions and customer support information

blockers.symptom: Authorization request fails because no code challenge was sent (community report: 'Missing required parameter: code_verifier')
blockers.cause: PKCE with S256 is mandatory for every OAuth app, so requests without a code challenge fail. A community user saw this error after switching the app's environment.
blockers.fix: Generate a verifier, derive an S256 challenge, and include it in the authorize request and the token exchange.

evidence.note: The exact error text comes from a community post, not official docs.

blockers.symptom: Production app rejects a callback URL that uses http
blockers.cause: Production redirect URIs must be https. Only Sandbox allows http on localhost.
blockers.fix: Use an https callback for Production, or test with a Sandbox app on localhost.

blockers.cause: The scope required by the endpoint was not requested at authorization, or the user declined it during install.
blockers.fix: Add the scope to the app and the authorize request, then have existing users re-authorize.

blockers.cause: The refresh token was already used. Refresh tokens are now single-use and rotate on each successful refresh.
blockers.fix: Overwrite the stored refresh token with the new one from every successful response. If the token is invalid, reauthorize the user.

blockers.symptom: Client secret is no longer visible
blockers.cause: Calendly does not show the client secret or webhook signing key after creation.
blockers.fix: Store them when the app is created. If lost, delete the app and create a new one (my inference from the documented delete option).

blockers.symptom: A connected user's token stops working
blockers.cause: Tokens are revoked if the account's login email, password or login method changes, or if the token is revoked manually.
blockers.fix: Detect the failure and send the user through reauthorization.

nuances.title: Token lifetimes
nuances.detail: Access tokens expire after 2 hours. Refresh tokens do not expire until used. Authorization codes expire after 10 minutes.

nuances.title: Refresh token rotation
nuances.detail: Refresh tokens are single-use. Each successful token request returns a new access token and a new refresh token, and the old refresh token is revoked immediately. Older pages that describe reusable refresh tokens are out of date.

evidence.note: Older Calendly pages say refresh tokens don't expire until used. The rotation guide adds single-use behavior.

nuances.title: Token request rate limit
nuances.detail: Only 8 OAuth tokens per user can be requested within one minute.

nuances.title: Per-user authorization
nuances.detail: Each connecting user gets a token for their own account. The token payload identifies the user and organization URIs.

nuances.title: Redirect URI must match exactly
nuances.detail: Enter exactly one redirect URI when creating the app, and send the same one in the authorize and token requests.

nuances.title: Webhooks need their own scopes
nuances.detail: Webhook subscriptions require webhooks:write to create them and webhooks:read to list them, and the related read scopes to receive payloads.
